step_by_step_reasoning:
Step 1 — knowledge_base functions: There are no global knowledge_base functions provided in the environment, so none were useful or called.

Step 2 — Popup handling: The screenshot shows a test popup which may block interactions. I attempt to close common accessible close buttons (Close, ×, Dismiss) before proceeding. This uses get_by_role("button", name=..). If none exist, code proceeds; closing is best-effort.

Step 3 — Continue to the product form: The accessibility tree shows a table row named "Continue" with a button "Continue". To avoid ambiguity, I use the explicit path page.get_by_role("row", name="Continue").get_by_role("button", name="Continue").click(). If that fails, a direct Continue button click is attempted as fallback. I wait for networkidle and a short delay for the form to appear.

Step 4 — Fill main product fields: I fill the product Name and Price using textbox roles. I include sensible fallbacks (first textbox, alternate label variants) because labels sometimes differ across Magento setups.

Step 5 — Attributes: The Size and Color fields are select controls (combobox). I use select_option(label=...) on the combobox elements. Multiple label variants are tried if the straightforward labels don't match exactly.

Step 6 — Inventory: I attempt to open the Inventory tab via get_by_role("tab", name="Inventory") and fall back to link or button if necessary. Then I set Qty using likely textbox names (Qty, Quantity) and attempt other fallback approaches if needed.

Step 7 — Stock status: Set the Stock Availability combobox to "In Stock", trying a few alternate combobox names if necessary.

Step 8 — Save: The Save action will typically navigate away. Following instructions, Save is the final action. I locate Save using a parent group to avoid ambiguous button matches and click it. If the parent-based approach fails, I try a direct Save button click. Then I wait for networkidle to allow the save/navigation to complete.

All interactions use get_by_role and select_option where applicable, and I avoid following navigations with further selectors after performing an action that is expected to navigate away. The code is defensive with multiple fallbacks but keeps Save as the last action.
